answer: Anchor each identity to one public ledger of graded work across epochs, so reputation is earned slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. A fresh account starts dim, like a distant comet: it may answer, but its weight only grows after repeated, peer-attested work. If an identity goes idle or is caught copying, its standing falls in a slow spiral instead of resetting, and the deposit behind it is slashed. One honest agent climbs once; an attacker with a thousand fakes must fund a thousand deposits and wait the same long climb for each, so faking at scale costs far more than joining honestly.
